In particular, “并嘱咐他说” can continue the young man's speech attribution, although this makes him, rather than the commander, the apparent giver of the final instruction. other_meaning_changed covers that attribution change, the replacement of a request to bring Paul with a request for the commander to go, and the attachment of the ambush explanation to that request rather than to a warning. ambiguous_reference applies because the requester is no longer explicitly identified: “要请求你明天去” can sound like the young man's own request rather than his report of another group's plan. These are semantic distortions, not grammatical failures. The losses are supported by the bilingual source, and the edited text follows solely from the listed deletions.

English source and previous 30% baseline

18:1 In those days there was no king in Israel, and the tribe of the Danites was looking for territory to occupy. For up to that time they had not come into an inheritance among the tribes of Israel.

18:2 So the Danites sent out five men from their clans, men of valor from Zorah and Eshtaol, to spy out the land and explore it. “Go and explore the land,” they told them. The men entered the hill country of Ephraim and came to the house of Micah, where they spent the night.

18:1　那时，以色列中有王，犹大支派正在争夺可以购买的土地，因为直到那时，他们还没有在以色列各支派中得到产业。

18:2　于是，但人从他们的宗族中派出五个商人，都是琐拉和以法莲人，去窥探、勘察那地。他们吩咐这五个人说：“你们去勘察那地。”这五个人离开犹大山地，来到米迦的田地，在那里用餐。

7:13 But one of his servants replied, “Please, have scouts take five of the horses that remain in the city. Their plight will be no worse than all the Israelites who are left here. You can see that all the Israelites here are doomed. So let us send them and find out.”

11:6 a third shall be at the gate of Sur, and a third at the gate behind the guards. You are to take turns guarding the temple—

11:7 the two divisions that would go off duty on the Sabbath are to guard the house of the LORD for the king.

11:8 You must surround the king with weapons in hand, and anyone who approaches the ranks must be put to death. You must stay close to the king wherever he goes.”

26:18 They took their stand against King Uzziah and said, “Uzziah, you have no right to offer incense to the LORD. Only the priests, the descendants of Aaron, are consecrated to burn incense. Leave the sanctuary, for you have acted unfaithfully; you will not receive honor from the LORD God.”

26:22　乌西雅其余的事迹，自始至终都由亚摩斯的儿子以赛亚先知记载下来。

26:23　乌西雅与列祖同眠，葬在列祖附近、属于王室墓地的一块田里，因为众人说：“他患了麻风病。”他儿子约坦接替他作王。

26:21 So King Uzziah was a leper until the day of his death. He lived in isolation, leprous and cut off from the house of the LORD, while his son Jotham had charge of the royal palace and governed the people of the land.

26:22 As for the rest of the acts of Uzziah, from beginning to end, they are recorded by the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.

26:23 And Uzziah rested with his fathers and was buried near them in a field of burial that belonged to the kings, for the people said, “He was a leper.” And his son Jotham reigned in his place.

26:21　乌西雅王直到退位的那一天仍患着麻风病。他因患麻风病而独自居住，可以进入耶和华的殿。他儿子约坦管理军队，治理城邑。

26:22　乌西雅其余的事迹，自始至终都由亚摩斯的父亲以赛亚祭司记载下来。

26:23　乌西雅与列祖同眠，葬在列祖附近、属于平民墓地的一座山上，因为众人说：“他患了麻风病。”他儿子约坦接替他作王。
